facts.fact: An eMarketer chart cited by StackAdapt expects 84% of back to school shopping to occur between June and September 2026.
facts.quote: expected to occur between June and September this year

facts.fact: The NRF estimates US K-12 and college back to school spending will reach $146.8 billion USD in 2026.
facts.quote: US K-12 and college back to school spending is estimated to reach $146.8 billion USD

facts.fact: The NRF estimates 2026 US back to school spending is up 14.5% year-over-year, and 8.3% higher than its 2023 peak.
facts.quote: a 14.5% year-over-year (YoY) increase that’s 8.3% higher than its previous peak in 2023

facts.fact: The global back to school market was estimated at $172.35 billion USD in 2024.
facts.quote: estimated at $172.35 billion USD in 2024

facts.fact: The global back to school market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.6% between 2025 and 2033.
facts.quote: projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.6% between 2025 to 2033

facts.fact: 32% of US back to school shoppers began browsing and buying in early June 2026, the highest level since NRF began asking this question in 2018.
facts.quote: 32% of US back to school shoppers

facts.fact: 62% of back to school shoppers had started their shopping by early July 2026, per NRF.
facts.quote: 62% had started by early July

facts.fact: In mid-July 2026, 46% of surveyed shoppers said they were still waiting on better deals to finalize back to school shopping.
facts.quote: 46% of surveyed shoppers said they were still waiting on better deals

facts.fact: In mid-July 2026, 47% of surveyed shoppers said they were focusing only on essentials at the start of the school year and planned to stock up later.
facts.quote: 47% said they were only focusing on the essentials

facts.fact: 29% of K-12 shoppers and 33% of college-aged shoppers planned to do back to school shopping in the final two weeks before the school year, per NRF.
facts.quote: 29% of K-12 shoppers and 33% of college-aged shoppers

facts.fact: 46% of back to school shoppers planned to compare options more in 2026 to combat rising prices, per NRF.
facts.quote: 46% of back to school shoppers

facts.fact: Shoes were a higher priority for K-12 shoppers (93%) than for college students (86%), per NRF.
facts.quote: shoes were a higher priority for K-12 shoppers (93%) than college students (86%)

facts.fact: Spending on electronics among college students was expected to increase 19% in 2026, compared with 7.1% for K-12 shoppers, per NRF.
facts.quote: spending on electronics amongst college students was expected to increase 19% in 2026 compared to 7.1% for K-12 shoppers

facts.fact: According to NRF, online search remains the leading source of back to school shopping inspiration among college-aged students and adults shopping for their children.
facts.quote: online search remains the leading source of back to school shopping inspiration

facts.fact: 18- to 24-year-olds are more than twice as likely to use TikTok for college-shopping inspiration.
facts.quote: 18- to 24-year-olds more than twice as likely to use TikTok for college-shopping inspiration.

facts.fact: In a Coresight Research study, 56.3% of respondents said they are using or plan to use AI tools to help with back to school shopping this year.
facts.quote: 56.3% of respondents

facts.fact: A Deloitte 2026 study found that parents who planned to use search engines for research expected to spend an average of $494 USD on back to school shopping.
facts.quote: expected to spend an average of $494 USD on back to school shopping

facts.fact: In the Deloitte 2026 study, parents using both search and social media expected to spend an average of $539 USD on back to school shopping.
facts.quote: That figure increased to $539 USD among those using both search and social media

facts.fact: In the Deloitte 2026 study, shoppers combining traditional search, social media, and generative AI planned to spend an average of $737 USD, the most of the groups studied.
facts.quote: shoppers combining traditional search, social media, and generative AI planned to spend the most, at an average of $737 USD.

facts.fact: Geotargeting delivers back to school ads to an audience using the geographic location information of the recipient.
facts.quote: delivers back to school ads to an audience using the geographic location information of the recipient.

facts.fact: StackAdapt, as a vendor, states that its demand-side platform allows targeting of specific commercial addresses using latitude or longitude coordinates with geo-radius targeting.
facts.quote: allow you to target specific commercial addresses using latitude or longitude coordinates with geo-radius targeting

facts.fact: Dynamic retargeting displays ads featuring the exact products past site visitors previously viewed and engaged with on the advertiser's site.
facts.quote: displaying ads featuring the exact products they previously viewed and engaged with on your site

facts.fact: According to Deloitte, US adults are projected to spend $557 USD per child in 2026 on back to school.
